title: Real-Time User Personalization & Contextual Bandit Recommendation Engine with Kafka Streaming, Redis Feature Store & Scikit-learn
problem: Generic static UI interfaces deliver lower user engagement, subpar conversion rates, and elevated bounce rates compared to dynamic personalized digital experiences. However, traditional batch-recomputed recommendation pipelines suffer from multi-hour stale recommendations, inability to capture intra-session user intent shifts, and crippling cold-start latency for newly launched items. This project builds a production-grade real-time personalization and contextual bandit recommendation engine in Python. The system ingests user interaction event streams over Apache Kafka, aggregates real-time session feature vectors in Redis with sub-millisecond retrieval, trains LinUCB and Thompson Sampling contextual bandit models with Scikit-learn, and serves personalized ranking recommendations via FastAPI with sub-18ms p95 latency.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Dynamic Product Listing Ranking
use_cases.first_sentence: Retail platforms need to re-rank search results and category listing carousels based on real-time item views and cart additions within the user's active session.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine consumes clickstream events via Kafka, updates the user's affinity vector in Redis, and computes personalized product re-rankings via FastAPI in under 15 milliseconds.

use_cases.title: Digital Media & News Feed Article Personalization
use_cases.first_sentence: Online news publishers need to balance showing trending breaking news articles against exploring newly published editorial pieces to discover reader preferences.
use_cases.second_sentence: The contextual bandit engine balances exploitation of known topic affinities with exploration of fresh content, maximizing long-term reader retention while avoiding stale filter bubbles.

use_cases.title: SaaS Onboarding Feature Discovery Recommendations
use_cases.first_sentence: Software product teams need to recommend relevant workflow templates and product tours to newly onboarded users based on their initial setup clicks.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system matches incoming user metadata with bandit feature vectors to recommend optimal onboarding actions, elevating free-to-paid activation rates.

hard_parts: Balancing exploitation of high-affinity items with algorithmic exploration of unvisited items using LinUCB upper confidence bounds
Maintaining low-latency sliding-window feature aggregation in Redis while consuming thousands of concurrent Kafka clickstream events
Managing cold-start penalties for new items with zero interaction history through feature fallback embeddings
Designing asynchronous offline batch model retraining in Celery that safely deploys updated bandit weight matrices to FastAPI without dropping live inference traffic
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating Kafka stream processors, Redis feature extractors, bandit math models, and FastAPI inference routers
Real-time benchmark proving sub-18ms p95 recommendation inference latency under 500 concurrent recommendation requests per second
Anti-fake verification script simulating an active user clicking 5 technology articles and asserting the recommendation distribution shifts toward technology within 300 milliseconds

components.name: Recommendation Throughput & Latency Benchmark Harness

components.name: Personalization Architecture Guide & Feature Store Schema

architecture.data_flow: A user clicks an item on the client UI; an engagement event publishes to the Kafka 'user-clicks' topic; the Kafka worker consumes the event and updates category view counters in Redis with a 30-minute sliding TTL; when the client requests personalized recommendations, FastAPI receives the user ID, executes an MGET against Redis to retrieve active session features in < 2ms, feeds the features into the LinUCB bandit scoring model, computes confidence bound scores for candidate items, filters previously viewed items, and returns top-K ranked item IDs; Celery periodically pulls historical conversion logs to retrain offline models.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Linear algebra ridge regression matrix inversion updates with L2 regularization preventing numerical divergence; bounded Redis memory TTLs.

prerequisites: Proficiency in Python asynchronous programming, FastAPI, and Scikit-learn
Understanding of message queues (Kafka), in-memory stores (Redis), and reinforcement learning / multi-armed bandit concepts

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU-based tabular bandit models and in-memory caches)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local Docker containers for Kafka and Redis)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Desktop (Kafka and Redis containers) and Python 3.11+
environment.fallback_path: In-memory Python queue and dictionary fallback store if Docker containers are unavailable

riskiest_component.name: Redis Memory Exhaustion and Cold-Start Latency Spikes
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce strict key expiration TTLs (30 minutes) on session vectors and pre-cache global popular item fallback lists.
riskiest_component.fallback: Tiered fallback returning top trending items when user session key is missing or Redis is unreachable.

deliverables: Git repository containing Kafka stream worker, Redis feature store client, LinUCB bandit engine, and FastAPI app
Docker Compose configuration launching single-node Kafka, Zookeeper/KRaft, and Redis instances
Automated benchmark harness measuring recommendation throughput, latency percentiles, and regret reduction
Screener verification script validating real-time preference adaptation and cold-start handling in under 2 minutes
out_of_scope: Third-party commercial CDPs or customer tracking cookies
Complex multi-billion parameter foundation LLM recommendation rankers
resources: A Contextual-Bandit Approach to Personalized News Recommendation (Li et al., WWW 2010)
Designing Machine Learning Systems: An Iterative Process for Production-Ready Applications (Chip Huyen)
Redis Documentation on Hashes, Sorted Sets, and Real-Time Feature Stores

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a real-time personalization engine with Kafka clickstream ingestion, Redis feature store, LinUCB bandit ranker, and FastAPI inference.
worksheet.q2: Target users: machine learning engineers, recommendation systems developers, and real-time data platform engineers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: e-commerce product re-ranking, digital news article personalization, and SaaS onboarding feature recommendations.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: exploration vs exploitation balance with LinUCB, sub-millisecond Redis session feature updates, cold-start handling, and non-blocking model retraining.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: Kafka event schemas, Redis feature store client, LinUCB implementation, and simulated clickstream generator. Synthetic data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero paid cloud keys. Fallback: in-memory queues and dictionaries.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Redis memory exhaustion and cold-start latency spikes. Fallback: 30-min key TTLs and tiered trending item fallbacks.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: returning hardcoded static recommendations. Anti-fake check 5 simulates 5 tech clicks and verifies top-3 output shifts to tech.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; strictly synthetic user interaction logs and simulated product IDs, zero personal data.
